summary: Chippewa County fire tower on Flambeau Ridge, begun 1931 and moved on the mountain in 1935-36; the Wisconsin list marks the 'first' entry gone, with no removal date found.

facts.design: Planned as a 100-foot steel observation tower with a six-foot steel house at the top
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association's Wisconsin list marks 'Flambeau Ridge – first' as Gone. A second Flambeau Ridge entry on the same list is marked Standing. The list does not say which structure each entry describes.
facts.agency: Wisconsin Conservation Commission (per 1931 to 1936 newspaper reports)

events.note: A newspaper report dated October 11, 1931 says the foundation for a 100-foot steel observation tower had been laid and the tower was being built as part of the reforestation program. No completion date is given.
A May 1932 newspaper report says the tower man installed there was on the job and had signaled for help for fires near Foster Lake.
A September 1935 report says the tower was being removed and moved farther north to a higher point on the mountain.
An April 1936 report says the tower was in its new location and ready for the fire permit season.

notes_for_editor: The brief is consistent with the list: 'Flambeau Ridge – first' is marked Gone. The list also has a second Flambeau Ridge entry marked Standing, about 0.7 km west by the listed coordinates (my calculation from the two coordinate pairs). Neither source ties either entry to the 1931-36 structures, so the story does not say which one the old tower is. The 1931-36 items are from a compilation of newspaper transcriptions (the page attributes them to the Eau Claire Leader and the Chippewa Herald-Telegram); I did not check the original papers. A 1975 newspaper item about a fall from the tower was left out, since it concerns a private person and adds nothing to the history. No source found gives a removal date or describes the site today. The story is about 310 words.
